slides.title: The backend checks the promise
slides.caption: demo.py · actual guard excerpt; message wrapped for the slide
slides.notes: This is the guard in our actual Apply implementation. It recomputes the plan immediately before mutation and compares it with the reviewed plan. A changed selection or edited plan must trigger another preview. The UI may disable Apply when it notices a change, but that is not sufficient protection: callers can invoke the backend directly. The backend therefore checks the promise independently. Ask students which other input belongs in the plan if they extend the operation to destination folders or material assignments.
slides.rationale: Pair the actual demo guard with the state model; connect an interface promise to backend enforcement.
slides.insight: The real implementation additionally checks label collisions and groups its mutations in an editor transaction. This excerpt isolates one responsibility and is not a standalone function.

slides.title: Recovery is observable behavior
slides.caption: Transaction excerpt from demo.py · loop and mutations omitted

slides.title: Mission Kontrol: repeatable testing
slides.credit: Etienne Palmer-Campbell · NetherRealm · GDC 2025 · PDF p.46
slides.notes: NetherRealm’s Mission Kontrol lets developers request actions without reproducing fighting-game input combinations. The game communicates the available move list to the tool, which avoids requiring the tester to memorize that list. This is an Unreal Slate and game-automation case, not Python editor scripting. The transferable design question is what knowledge the interface can supply at the moment it is needed. In our peer test, provide a reproducible starting state and an observable goal so we can evaluate the tool rather than the reviewer’s memory.

slides.title: Feedback changes the interface
slides.credit: Etienne Palmer-Campbell · NetherRealm · GDC 2025 · PDF p.47

slides.title: Peer testing: three perspectives
slides.question: What will you observe before suggesting a redesign?
slides.notes: Work in groups of four with three reciprocal rounds. The diagram separates the facilitator’s actions from the participant’s task. For our lab, use the author’s machine and the prepared input. Let the partner attempt the goal before coaching; record any assistance. If the tool cannot run, switch promptly to the declared prototype or recording mode. That review can still reveal interpretation problems, but it cannot establish runtime correctness.
